chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Exchange gifts, you will love one another; exchange gifts, for they remove enmity.'

key_terms.تَحَابُّوا: Love one another / become mutually loving

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of exchanging gifts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith emphasizes the Prophetic tradition of using gift-giving as a practical mechanism to dissolve grudges and cultivate affection, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on social harmony. Scholars note that the repetition of 'tahādaw' (exchange gifts) underscores its importance as a proactive social duty rather than a mere custom, aligning with the Quranic principle of maintaining brotherhood and unity among believers.
